prompt: CHALLENGE: Why must radical chlorination of methane use EXCESS methane (CH₄ as the limiting reactant for Cl₂, not the other way around)?

options.label: Once CH₃Cl forms, it still has 3 C–H bonds that Cl• can abstract. With limited CH₄, further chlorination gives CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃, CCl₄ — a mix of over-halogenated products.
The reaction is too exothermic without excess.

explanation: Each halogenation product (CH₃Cl, CH₂Cl₂, CHCl₃) still has abstractable H's — they can all keep reacting with Cl•. With excess CH₄, Cl• statistically hits unreacted methane most often. Industrial production of CHCl₃ or CCl₄ deliberately uses the opposite ratio to drive over-halogenation.
